extracted.intended_audience: Potential offerors (academia, industry, research community) preparing white papers or full proposals in response to the ONR Long Range BAA (N00014-24-S-B001)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for preparing and submitting white papers and full proposals to the Office of Naval Research (ONR) Long Range Broad Agency Announcement for Navy and Marine Corps S&T. Covers eligibility, format, content, registration, evaluation criteria, contract/grant/OTA instrument rules, and administrative requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for Competition
rubrics_metrics.description: All responsible sources from academia, industry and the research community worldwide may submit proposals under this BAA; HBCUs/MIs, small and large businesses are encouraged. FFRDCs and certain DoD/civilian labs and Navy labs/military universities/warfare centers are not eligible to receive awards (teaming arrangements allowed if permitted). UARCs eligible unless precluded by their DoD UARC contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teams are encouraged; offerors must be willing to cooperate and exchange software, data and other information in integrated programs selected by ONR. Disclosures of current and pending support may render an applicant ineligible; DoD may request updates throughout performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and Treatment of Contracted Fundamental Research
rubrics_metrics.description: ONR follows USD(AT&L) guidance: 'contracted fundamental research' includes work funded by RDT&E Budget Activity 1 (Basic Research) or Budget Activity 2 (Applied Research) performed on-campus at a university. Other applied research not on-campus, Budget Activity 3, or 4 do not meet the definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ONR will place no restriction on conduct/reporting of unclassified contracted fundamental research except as required by statute/regulation/EO. Prime contractor must identify and confirm any subcontracted unclassified research that is fundamental research. Consult ONR Technical POCs to determine classification. Some applied research may be restricted and require DoD pre-publication review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument Type(s) and their Characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards may be contracts, grants, cooperative agreements, and other transaction agreements (OTAs). Grants: transfer of value to carry out a public purpose; substantial involvement not expected; no fee/profit. Cooperative agreements: like grants but substantial involvement expected; no fee/profit. OTAs for Research and Prototypes have statutory bases (10 U.S.C. §4021/4022) and special cost-share/non-duplication features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors should understand differences (e.g., government involvement, fee/profit restrictions) and consult provided guide links. OTAs for research generally expect 50/50 cost share 'to the maximum extent practicable' and must not duplicate existing DoD efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: White Paper Format Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: White Paper Format: 8.5 x 11-inch paper; 1-inch margins; single-spaced; Times New Roman, 12 point; page limit – 5 pages excluding cover page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FedConnect will not accept a white paper unless the mandatory Cover Page is included. When email submission is required, files must be Word 2016 or PDF compatible and email size limit is 5MB.

rubrics_metrics.name: White Paper Required Content Elements
rubrics_metrics.description: White papers must include: Cover Page (MANDATORY for ONR and ONRG), Technical Concept, Future Naval Relevance, Operational Naval Concept (where applicable), Operational Utility Assessment Plan (where applicable), and a Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) cost estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover Page templates/links provided; Program Officer information required on cover page. For ONRG, a Science Director is required on the cover. Offerors should consult the cognizant Program Officer regarding desirability of white paper submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full Proposal Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Full proposals must follow the instructions in Appendix 1 (Grants and Cooperative Agreements) or Appendix 2 (Contracts and OTAs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific formatting/content and submission instructions (including any additional appendices or attachments) are in those appendices; offerors must follow the instrument-specific instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission Portals and Registration Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions may be through Grants.gov, SAM.gov (Contract Opportunities), ONR website, and FedConnect (for white papers). All entities submitting a proposal through FedConnect must register with SAM and have a Unique Entity Identifier (UEI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors must be registered in SAM prior to submission, provide a valid UEI, and maintain an active SAM registration while an award is active or a proposal is under consideration. Failure to register may disqualify an applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and SAM Maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: All offerors must be registered in SAM prior to submission, provide a valid unique entity identifier, and maintain an active SAM registration with current information during any active Federal award or application under consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Federal awarding agency may not make an award until the applicant has complied with all UEI and SAM requirements; noncompliance can be a basis to make an award to another applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security Classification of Submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: White Papers and Proposals are expected to be unclassified; classified submissions are permitted, but any classified proposal selected for award must be accompanied by an unclassified Statement of Work (SOW).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classified proposals must be submitted to ONR’s Document Control Unit with specific outer/inner envelope addressing and markings as described. Do not put proprietary markings in or on the Statement of Work; a non-proprietary SOW must also be submitted for all proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Proprietary Statement of Work and Proprietary Marking
rubrics_metrics.description: A non-proprietary version of the Statement of Work must be submitted for all proposals; do not put proprietary data or markings in or on the Statement of Work. For data an offeror wishes to restrict, the proposal title page must include a specific restrictive legend and each restricted sheet must be marked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific legend text is provided in the BAA and must be used. The Government’s right to use information if awarded is described in the legend. Mark each sheet to be restricted with the specified legend to ensure evaluation-only handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proprietary Data Legend and Marking Instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: For proposals containing data the offeror does not want disclosed, the title page must include a specified legend declaring data shall not be disclosed outside the Government except for evaluation, and each sheet to be restricted must be marked with a sheet-level legend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exact legend language is provided in the announcement; failure to follow the marking instructions may result in loss of restriction or mishandling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Titles Should Be Descriptive
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles given to submissions should be descriptive of the work they cover and not merely a copy of the title of this announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Descriptive titles help routing and identification by Program Officers and reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of Late Proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government reserves the right not to review proposals submitted after 30 September 2024 (or after a successor BAA is issued), or otherwise per the Key Dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors should submit within the recommended dates in the BAA Calls and check the ONR/SAM/Grants.gov postings for call-specific deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Confidentiality and Non-Return Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical and cost proposals (or any other material) submitted will not be returned and are treated as sensitive competitive information; contents disclosed only for evaluation purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ONR treats submissions as sensitive competitive information and will disclose content only as needed for evaluation under applicable law/regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary Selection Criteria (FAR 35.016(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary basis for selection: technical merit, importance to agency programs, and funds availability. Cost realism and reasonableness will also be considered when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ONR reserves the right to request additional information after instrument type determination and to remove offerors who fail to reach agreement on award terms, conditions, and cost/price in a reasonable time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Criterion 1 — Scientific and Technical Merit
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall scientific and technical merits and responsiveness: degree of innovation, soundness of technical concept, Offeror's awareness of the state of the art and understanding of the problem scope, significance and originality of the technical approach, and anticipated scientific impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also considered: (A) Offeror’s capabilities, related experience, facilities, techniques or unique combinations integral to achieving objectives; and (B) qualifications, capabilities and experience of PI, team leader, and key personnel critical to achieving objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Criterion 2 — Potential Naval Relevance and Contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential Naval relevance and contribution to ONR and Department of Navy mission, including consideration of protection of intellectual property, controlled information, key personnel, and critical technologies; and limiting undue influence including foreign talent programs that may attempt to exploit U.S. technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consideration will be given to improper technology transfer, IP theft, cyber or human espionage, entities known to recruit for transfers, misleading information or concealed connections; offerors should disclose and mitigate risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Criterion 3 — Availability of Funds
rubrics_metrics.description: The availability of funds is a selection criterion (not applicable to white papers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per NDAA 2021 Section 1062, beginning Oct 1, 2024, DoD may not fund institutions hosting a Confucius Institute unless waived; such statutory constraints may affect awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal Weighting of Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria 1 (Scientific/Technical Merit), 2 (Naval Relevance), and 3 (Availability of Funds) are equally important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors should address all three criteria in their proposals; omission/weakness in any may affect selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and Selection Process Characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals will not be evaluated against each other (no common work statement); ONR intends to review as soon as possible after arrival but may review periodically. Scientific/technical community makes recommendations forwarded to Contracts and Grants Awards Management. Recommendation does not guarantee award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After selection, Contracting/Grant office conducts cost analysis, responsibility determinations, fund availability checks, and other steps. Offerors may be required to demonstrate compliance with enhanced cybersecurity requirements prior to award.

rubrics_metrics.name: No Reimbursement for Proposal Development Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: ONR provides no funding for direct reimbursement of proposal development costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors should budget their own proposal development expenses; funds will not be paid to cover those costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Sharing / Matching Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost sharing is not expected under contracts and assistance awards and will not be used as a factor during merit review; voluntary cost sharing may be considered. OTAs may expect cost share (see OTA guidance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to 2 CFR 200.306 and FAR 35.003 for additional guidance; OTAs under 10 U.S.C. §4021/4022 commonly expect 50/50 cost share 'to the maximum extent practicable'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcontracting Plan Requirement for Contracts > $750,000
rubrics_metrics.description: For proposed contract awards exceeding $750,000, large businesses and non-profits (including educational institutions) shall provide a Subcontracting Plan containing all elements required by FAR 19.704 and FAR 52.219-9, as supplemented by DFARS 252.219-7003. Small businesses are exempt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Plan must be an attachment to the Proposal Checklist and will not count in page limits. If a Master or Individual Subcontracting Plan exists, include a copy. Plans are reviewed for adequacy; failure to negotiate an acceptable Plan may make the apparent successful offeror ineligible for award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcontracting Plan Goals and Justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors shall propose a plan ensuring small business categories (SDBs, WOSBs, HUBZone, VOSBs, SDVOSBs) have the maximum practicable opportunity to participate consistent with efficient performance. If proposed goals lack positive goals or SDB goals are below 5%, a written explanation is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors should propose realistic goals and document outreach/attempts to include small businesses; include explanations when goals are limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcontracting Resources and Outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: ONR provides (and references) lists of resources to help locate subcontracting partners (DSBS, SAM opportunities, Navy SBIR/STTR Search, SBA Subnet, USAspending, DAU SB COP, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors pursuing subcontracting should use these resources to maximize small business participation and compliance with subcontracting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational Conflict of Interest (OCI) Disclosure and Certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors must disclose any past, present, or planned interests that may create an OCI (financial, contractual, organizational, personal) and certify disclosure. Failure to disclose may result in disqualification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The BAA provides required certification language and outlines potential Government actions if OCI exists (impose conditions, disqualify, include mitigation in award, or seek waiver).

rubrics_metrics.name: OCI Mitigation Plan Minimum Contents
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicable, a Mitigation Plan must at minimum: (i) provide organizational charts showing structure relative to performance and relevant contracts; (ii) demonstrate isolation of elements creating OCI from performance resources; (iii) show geographic/physical separation if appropriate; (iv) describe personnel reassignment processes and restrictions; (v) describe controls including NDAs over future employment; (vi) describe OCI training for employees; (vii) provide evidence supporting mitigation assertions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Contracting Officer will review certifications/statements/mitigation plans and may require additional information. If accepted, the Mitigation Plan becomes part of the contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAR/DFARS/NMCARS Clause Compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicable FAR/DFARS/NMCARS provisions and clauses (many listed by number in the BAA) may apply to awards; ONR reserves the right to include any relevant/current clauses necessary for the final award based on award value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors must be familiar with and comply with referenced clauses (e.g., SAM requirements, cyber clauses, TINA, prohibition on certain telecommunications equipment, trafficking, export/China-related clauses, etc.). Links to acquisition.gov are provided for clause texts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth in Negotiations Act (TINA) / Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data
rubrics_metrics.description: All proposals submitted under this BAA that meet the TINA threshold are subject to certified cost and pricing data; offerors are required to execute the Certificate of Current Cost or Pricing Data as soon as practicable but no later than five business days after date of price agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost/pricing data submitted after price agreement will be reviewed post-award to determine if certified data up to price agreement was defective and whether price adjustments are due under FAR 52.215-10/11.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced Cybersecurity / CUI Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain performers may be required to implement enhanced cybersecurity controls to unclassified networks housing Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) per NMCARS 52.204.7303 in addition to DFARS 252.204-7012/7018. Offerors may be required to demonstrate compliance prior to award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors are strongly encouraged to consult the cognizant Program Officer to determine whether enhanced controls will apply to a particular effort and to be prepared for assessment/requirements (NIST SP 800-171 references).

rubrics_metrics.name: OTAs — Non-Duplication and Follow-on Production Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: OTAs must not be duplicative of effort conducted under existing DoD programs. Under 10 U.S.C. §4022, ONR may award a follow-on production contract or OTA if participants successfully completed the prototype and the OTA provides for follow-on award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors considering OTAs should consult the DoD OTA guides and ensure the effort is not duplicative; OTAs may include follow-on production provisions and cost-share expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representations Regarding Covered Telecommunications and Related Disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerors must make representations about providing or using covered telecommunications equipment/services (per Section 889) and disclose vendor/manufacturer details if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The BAA includes representation language and required disclosure fields (entity, CAGE, model numbers, item descriptions, proposed use). Offerors should review SAM excluded parties and be prepared to disclose covered equipment/services details if 'will' or 'does' responses selected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced Security Controls on Select Defense Industrial Base Partner Networks
rubrics_metrics.description: ONR may require enhanced cybersecurity controls on unclassified networks hosting CUI for select programs; determination made by the Chief of Naval Research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerors should consult Program Officers, and be aware these controls are additional to DFARS 252.204-7012 (e.g., NIST SP 800-171 assessment requirements, potential added controls per NMCARS 52.204.7303).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of Recommended Proposals — No Guarantee of Award
rubrics_metrics.description: A notification that a full proposal has been recommended indicates selection in accordance with evaluation criteria and referral to the Contracting Department, but does not guarantee award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsequent steps include cost analysis, responsibility determination, funding confirmation, and any other pre-award actions; failure to reach agreement on terms/price/time may remove an offeror from award consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: White Paper Submission Logistics and FedConnect Registration/Support
rubrics_metrics.description: ONR uses FedConnect for white paper submission in many cases; registration with SAM and FedConnect account creation are required, and FedConnect has support resources and a 'Ready Set Go' guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use the FedConnect Message Center to submit questions or white papers; use the POCs identified in Section G. FedConnect support contact information and hours are provided.
